queries.query: This feature branch picked up a pile of AI narration comments while we iterated: step-by-step 'now we loop over the items' lines and a commented-out old implementation. Strip the low-value comments before I open the PR.
Can you check whether the tests in the pricing package actually prove anything? I suspect a few of them can't fail no matter what the code does.
Decomment src/billing/ for me. Keep the license headers and anything explaining an upstream bug, but the rest of the chatter has to go.

Some of the tests in the auth module look tautological to me, like comparing a value with itself or only asserting that a mock was called. Find the ones that prove nothing and confirm it by mutating the code.
Go through the comments in the files I changed on this branch and remove the ones that just narrate what the code does. Every comment that survives should explain a constraint we can't change.
Our ledger tests have been green for two years and I'm no longer convinced they would catch a regression. Find out which of them would still pass if the code they test were broken.
We're adding a refund-window check to the orders service. Write the failing test for the 30-day cutoff first, then implement the check until it passes.
Review PR #512 for bugs and security problems before I merge it; the session-token handling in the middleware is what worries me most.
Users are randomly getting a 500 from the search endpoint since yesterday afternoon. Find the root cause before anyone touches the code.
The README for the CLI is months out of date. Refresh it against the current commands and flags, and fix the installation section.
Run a mutation-testing tool across the whole repo and give me the overall mutation score and kill ratio for the quarterly quality report.

The comment above the retry helper in client.go says the 37 ms sleep works around a load-balancer quirk. Explain why that comment says what it says: dig through the history and tell me where the number came from.
There's a lot of commented-out code and 'TODO: this is a hack' notes in the scheduler. Clean up the comments so only the ones that earn their place are left.
I want proof, not opinions: which of the tests in internal/rates would keep passing if someone changed the rounding logic? Use mutation to show it.
Run a decomment pass over the files touched on this branch; the agent that wrote them narrated every line.
Check whether the tests I added to the cart package this week prove anything. A couple of them feel like they'd pass even if the code were wrong.
Write a test for the new discount-code parser that covers stacked codes and an expired code.
Review the diff on this branch before I merge it. I'm worried about the error handling in the uploader.
TestCheckoutTotals started failing after this morning's merge and nobody knows why. Debug it and find what broke.
Delete the dead code in legacy/. Nothing has called those helpers since the v2 API shipped.
